description.value: The study investigated structural brain alterations associated with cancer-related PTSD and examined the longitudinal course of gray matter volume over 2 years.

spans.text: We investigated brain structural alterations and the longitudinal courses in patients with cancer-related PTSD.

design.value: Baseline and 2-year follow-up structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry, comparing breast cancer survivors with PTSD, survivors without PTSD, and healthy subjects, with a longitudinal diagnosis-by-time analysis.

spans.text: Baseline scans using magnetic resonance imaging were performed in 14 cancer survivors with PTSD, 100 without PTSD, and 70 healthy subjects. Follow-up scans were performed 2 years later in 76 cancer survivors (PTSD, n=9; non-PTSD, n=67).

To measure the PTSD symptomatic responses to the cancer experience, the Impact of Event Scale (IES), which is used worldwide to assess PTSD symptomatic responses to specific traumatic experiences, was used.

description.value: A self-reported questionnaire consisting of 15 items: 7 items assessing intrusion symptoms and 8 items assessing avoidance symptoms. Each item is rated using a 4-point scale (“not at all” = 0, “rarely” = 1, “sometimes” = 3, “often” = 5).

description.value: Images were spatially normalized to a customized study-specific template, segmented into gray and white matter, modulated to correct for volume changes during normalization, and smoothed using 8-mm and then 12-mm FWHM Gaussian kernels.

spans.text: All the scans were spatially normalized to the customized template, then smoothed with an 8-mm, full-width maximum (FWHM) smoothing kernel, followed by averaging to create a customized template. The images were then segmented into gray matter and white matter, using customized prior probability maps. These segments were then modulated to correct for volume changes occurring during spatial normalization. Finally, the images were smoothed using a 12-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.
